title: PostgreSQL Read Committed vs. Repeatable Read Isolation Levels
realWorldScenario: An analytical report queries customer balances at 10:00 AM, then executes a second query at 10:01 AM inside the same transaction. The second query returns different numbers because other users made payments in the interim.
questionStatement: Explain why this Non-Repeatable Read anomaly occurs under PostgreSQL's default `Read Committed` isolation level. How does `Repeatable Read` prevent this using snapshot isolation?
hints: Does a transaction see commits that happened after the transaction started, or after each statement started?
